sourceCopy.name: Bcrypt Generator
sourceCopy.title: Bcrypt Generator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Create and verify bcrypt password hashes locally with a fresh random salt and adjustable cost. Free browser tool; no upload or account.
sourceCopy.intro: Generate a standard bcrypt hash or check a password against an existing bcrypt hash. Work runs in a local browser worker, and the password is cleared after each check.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: What does a bcrypt hash do?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Bcrypt is a password-hashing function, not encryption. It combines a one-way hash with a random salt and a configurable work factor. A hash can be checked against a candidate password but cannot be decrypted to reveal the original.
sourceCopy.privacyQuestion: Are my password or hash uploaded or saved?
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. Hashing and verification run in this browser. The page does not send the entered password or hash to a server or save them; the password field is cleared when the operation finishes. For safety, use a test password rather than a real account password.

fields.accuracyNote: Bcrypt uses only the first 72 UTF-8 bytes. This tool rejects longer values rather than silently truncating them. Cost 8–14 increases work exponentially; higher costs can take longer, especially on phones. A local worker keeps the page responsive, but your device performs the work.
fields.privacyNote: Use a test password, not a real login password. The result is for learning and compatibility checks; do not use this browser page as a production account-storage system.
fields.verifyHint: Paste a standard 60-character bcrypt hash. Verification supports bcrypt costs 4–14; unusually high-cost hashes are declined to avoid unbounded work on your device.

additionalFaqs.question: Does bcrypt encrypt my password?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. Bcrypt is a one-way password hash, not reversible encryption. It is designed to let software check a candidate password without storing the original password.

additionalFaqs.question: Why does bcrypt have a 72-byte limit?
additionalFaqs.answer: The bcrypt format processes at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. This tool refuses longer input so different passwords are never silently treated as the same truncated value.

additionalFaqs.question: Should I store this hash for a real account?
additionalFaqs.answer: Do not use this page as a production credential system. Real services should hash passwords on their trusted server with maintained authentication libraries, suitable parameters, rate limits and account protections.
